title: The day before: a ketamine overdose at the Chi Phi house
summary: [ABC News](abc) reports that someone overdosed on ketamine at the Chi Phi house the day before the party.

title: Sorority pregame, then Moonies and Lot 10
summary: After drinking Tito's vodka at the Tri Delta house, Doe took an Uber at about 8:30 p.m. to the chapter's event at Moonies Bar & Nightclub, accompanied by the sorority's house mother. Bouncers marked both her hands with an "X" because she was under 21, but the complaint says she was still served ([¶¶ 136–139](complaint@23)).
At about 10 p.m. she and other sisters walked to Lot 10 Bar and Lounge, where she was given an under-21 wristband ([¶¶ 141–142](complaint@24)). Moonies is a defendant under New York's Dram Shop Act.

title: Arrives alone at the Chi Phi house
summary: She "stumbled alone" to 107 Edgemoor Lane to see Matthew Ingalls, visibly intoxicated after about ten drinks in three hours ([¶¶ 143–144](complaint@24)). Members at the door let her in. Ingalls gave her a beer, danced with her, and proposed a threesome with another brother ([¶¶ 145–148](complaint@24)).
The complaint says Ingalls led her upstairs, left her with another member, then brought her to a room where Johnathan Newell was sitting on a couch ([¶¶ 150–151](complaint@25)).

title: Ketamine, marijuana and liquor; the first alleged assaults
summary: According to the complaint, Ingalls and Newell passed around a bag of a white powder said to be ketamine and pressured her to snort it, though she had never used it. They also gave her marijuana and a high-proof "Jamaican Liquor" ([¶¶ 152–154](complaint@25)).

The complaint alleges that Ingalls forced oral sex on her while Newell forced intercourse and slapped her hard enough to bruise. Ingalls then went to sleep on a bed. Gillio Lopes came in, and he and Newell put her on a bed and assaulted her ([¶¶ 155–161](complaint@25)).

title: The "Chi Phi Actives" Snapchat group
summary: The complaint alleges that at about 1:42 a.m. Newell posted in the chapter's Snapchat group that there was "free pussy" upstairs, which "organized and encouraged other XI CHAPTER members to join" ([¶¶ 162–163](complaint@26)). [Page 27 of the complaint](complaint@27) reproduces a photo of a phone showing the thread, with the status-bar clock reading 2:37.
Below is everything legible in that photo, top to bottom. Sender names are the Snapchat display names shown on screen. Apart from the 1:42 a.m. post, the complaint does not say who wrote which reply.

Campus investigators also found that a photo of Doe was shared among active members in a Snapchat group that night. The documents do not describe the photo. The thread reached investigators anonymously, and Cornell's attorneys, in a July 17 memo filed in Kretzschmar's court challenge, said it "became a key exhibit" in the conduct case ([NBC](nbc)).

title: Members enter the room; ketamine poured over her body
summary: The complaint says several more members then came in. She hid under the covers, her phone out of reach across the room. Diego Sarabia grabbed her face and kissed her until she pushed him away ([¶¶ 164–166](complaint@28)).

Newell allegedly made her snort a line of ketamine off his body. Then, as she lay on the bed, all seven defendants (Ingalls, Newell, Lee, Lopes, Sarabia, Norris and Kretzschmar) allegedly poured lines of ketamine over her and snorted them ([¶¶ 167–169](complaint@28)).

title: Her roommate checks in
summary: [The New York Times](nyt) reports a text from her roommate at 3:05 a.m. Doe answered at 3:09 a.m. that she wasn't sure. The Times did not quote her reply.

title: Moved to a second room; loses consciousness
summary: According to the complaint, the other five left, and Ingalls and Winston Lee took her to a smaller room believed to be the chapter president's office. There they gave her more ketamine and, while she was "completely incapacitated," forced oral and vaginal sex on her at the same time. The assault ended at about 5:45 a.m., when she lost consciousness ([¶¶ 170–174](complaint@28)).

title: Back at the sorority house
summary: The complaint says she woke in shock and went back to the Tri Delta house, where she found a large bruise on her buttocks and took medication for a UTI. That day she learned the night was "becoming public knowledge" on campus ([¶¶ 175–178](complaint@29)).

title: Newell apologizes by text
summary: The day after, Newell texted her an apology. Her reply described the night as legal.

title: Welcomed, then disinvited; she learns about the group chat
summary: Ingalls told her she was still welcome at Chi Phi. The chapter president then called to disinvite her from the Halloween party ([NYT](nyt)).

Around this time she learned how many men had been involved. [CBS](cbs-texts) reports she saw online comments about an alleged gang rape. Her lawyer, Thomas Giuffra, told [NBC News](nbc) she learned of the Snapchat messages only when another fraternity member, outraged by what his brothers were said to have done, leaked them to her.

title: Police report; chapter and all seven temporarily suspended
summary: Encouraged by friends, she reported to the Cornell University Police Department. The same day Cornell put the Xi Chapter on temporary suspension and temporarily suspended all seven men, who the complaint says were allowed to mitigate their conduct by submitting essays ([¶¶ 179–181](complaint@29)). Cornell denies that essays were ever the only consequence ([Cornell FAQ](cu-faq); [Daily Sun](sun-essays)).

title: CUPD interviews
summary: Over two days she gave Cornell police an interview that produced a [transcript of about 120 pages](cupd-transcript), saying, "I can say with 100% confidence I was raped" ([CBS](cbs-texts)). Investigators also prepared a [six-page sworn statement](sworn-statement).

title: District Attorney declines to prosecute
summary: Tompkins County District Attorney Matthew Van Houten declined to bring charges. He relied on the [six-page sworn statement](sworn-statement), which he says described the conduct as "voluntary, conscious, and consensual," and he says he never saw the full interview transcript ([DA statement](da); [CBS](cbs-details)).

title: Cornell's public statement
summary: In a [statement](cu-2024) titled "Update on disturbing allegations of sexual violence," Interim President Michael I. Kotlikoff addressed "serious and deeply disturbing allegations of drug abuse and sexual violence" at Chi Phi. The chapter remained under the suspension issued November 8 ([¶ 182](complaint@29)).

title: Title IX investigation opens
summary: Cornell's Title IX office opened an investigation in response to her formal complaint ([¶ 183](complaint@29)).

title: Presidential task force on campus sexual assault
summary: Cornell created a presidential task force on campus sexual assault ([ABC](abc)).

title: Title IX hearings and outcomes
summary: Cornell held at least twelve hearings ([¶ 184](complaint@30)), drawing on about 50 interviews ([ABC](abc)). President Kotlikoff later gave the outcomes: two students expelled, two suspended for at least two semesters, two found not responsible for sexual misconduct, and one who had already graduated ([CBS](cbs-details)).

Citing federal privacy law, Cornell has not said which outcome applied to whom ([Cornell FAQ](cu-faq)). [NBC](nbc) reports that Scott Kretzschmar was found responsible for "attempted sexual exploitation."

title: Campus sexual misconduct survey
summary: Cornell's 2025 survey found that 35% of undergraduate women reported nonconsensual sexual contact. The complaint cites the survey ([¶ 185](complaint@30)).

title: Civil complaint filed in New York County
summary: The 101-page [complaint](complaint@1) is dated September 14, 2026 ([p. 101](complaint@101)). Some outlets, including [ABC](abc) and [TIME](time), report a filing date of September 16. Its [caption](complaint@3) names Cornell; Chi Phi's chapter house association, national fraternity and educational trust; Delta Delta Delta and its Alpha Beta house corporation; Moonies; former chapter president Orazio Petito; John Doe faculty, alumni and executive-board members; and the seven men.

The complaint pleads causes of action for negligence; negligent retention and supervision; breach of contract; violations of the New York State Human Rights Law; sexual assault; sexual battery; intentional and negligent infliction of emotional distress; and violations of the Dram Shop Act. It seeks compensatory and punitive damages and a jury trial ([prayer for relief](complaint@100)).

title: DA reopens the case for a grand jury
summary: Van Houten [assigned](da) a senior sex-crimes prosecutor to present the case to a grand jury. He says his office never received the group-chat image. Plaintiff's counsel says it was given to authorities in 2024 ([NPR](npr)).

title: Cornell FAQ; independent review
summary: Cornell published an [FAQ](cu-faq) saying the Snapchat screenshot had been given to the DA, which the DA disputes. Cornell later edited the FAQ ([Daily Sun](sun-faq)). Gov. Kathy Hochul called for an independent review, and Cornell agreed to retain outside counsel ([ABC](abc); [CBS](cbs-details)).

title: Attorney General named special prosecutor
summary: By executive order, Gov. Hochul made New York Attorney General Letitia James special prosecutor, with authority to investigate and, if warranted, prosecute ([Daily Sun](sun-ag); [CBS](cbs-details)).
